questions.question: What happens if a player needs to draw a new hand and both the cosmic deck and discard pile are empty?
questions.ruling_summary: If a required cosmic-deck draw cannot be made because both deck and discard are empty, everyone discards and is dealt eight after reshuffling (Cosmic Quake). If insufficient, Cosmic Aftershock discards all cosmic cards including Miser's hoard; setup card holdings are replenished. Omit expansion reward cards, Cryo, Cyborg and The Claw.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Cosmic Quake! Each player discards all of their cards, and the discard pile is shuffled to make a new deck, then 8 cards are dealt to each player. If after performing a Cosmic Quake there still aren’t enough cards to deal out a full hand to each player, then a Cosmic Aftershock occurs.  All cosmic deck cards (and reward deck cards) are discarded (including Miser’s hoard, Cryo’s deep freeze, etc.).  Game Setup effects like Cyborg and The Claw get to replenish as if starting the game.

questions.question: What happens if a Cosmic Quake does not free up enough cards?
questions.ruling_summary: If Quake is insufficient, discard and reshuffle all cards; redeal setup holdings such as Miser's hoard.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: If a Cosmic Quake does not free up enough cards, all cards are discarded and shuffled together. Any alien powers that start the game with 1 or more cards (such as Miser’s hoard) are dealt those cards now.

questions.question: What if a player is taking rewards from the reward deck while there is no cosmic deck or discard pile? Does a Cosmic Quake still occur?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The Cosmic Quake is only triggered when a player needs to draw from the cosmic deck and there are no cards available.

questions.question: When should alert levels on aliens be mixed?
questions.ruling_summary: Learn with green aliens without flares, add flares, then yellow and red aliens as experience grows; alert level measures required experience rather than strength.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: It is recommended that players start with green aliens only with no flares when first playing, then add flares. Play a couple of games, then introduce yellows to the green alert. Play a few more games with those, then add the red level aliens. The alert level is not how powerful they are, but how experienced your group should be to include them in the game.

questions.question: Do I receive compensation if my ships do not go to the warp (because I am the Zombie or because I lost to the Void, for instance)?
questions.ruling_summary: Compensation requires ships actually lost to the warp; Zombie prevention and Void eradication do not qualify.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. You only receive compensation for ships you lose to the warp.

questions.question: What is the difference between “lost” ships, “losing” ships, and ships “sent” to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Lost ships go to the warp involuntarily; losing ships are those involved that should go there; sent ships result from specific actions and count as lost. Observer covers all three; Void eradicates losing ships. Expansion-specific Fungus/Remote behavior is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Lost ships are any that go to the warp involuntarily at any point in the encounter. Losing ships are those involved in the encounter (main player or allies) that should go to the warp. Sent ships are those that go to the warp because of a specific player action (power or effect), sometimes voluntarily, but not directly involved in the encounter, and count as lost. Remote “sends” ships to the warp, and those ships are “lost” to the warp (but are not “losing” ships). Zombie’s ships would be “losing” ships, but are not “lost” to the warp. Fungus captures losing ships, so would not capture ships lost to Grudge. Observer would protect losing ships, and those lost or sent. Note that Void specifically eradicates losing ships rather than sending them to the warp (this is why Zombie’s ships are eradicated, and why Fungus would not capture losing ships as Void’s ally).

questions.question: Is a ship still considered “sent to the warp” or “lost to the warp” if an effect interrupts its arrival to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Ships prevented from reaching the warp are not lost/sent to it; Healer cannot heal Zombie ships that never arrive. Ghoul/capture examples are excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: No. Therefore, Healer can only heal, and Ghoul can only feast if the ships actaully reach the warp. This is why Healer doesn’t normally heal Zombie, and Ghoul does not feast on captured ships.

questions.question: Does reclaiming an empty planet in your home system count as a win?
questions.ruling_summary: Reclaiming an empty home planet is a win and a successful encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes. It is a win, and a successful encounter.

questions.question: Can you always interrupt an effect to do something else? As an example, playing a flare in response to compensation, or an effect like a Finder artifact?
questions.ruling_summary: Resolve an effect completely before another, except a Zap or explicit interrupt. Use timing rules for simultaneous effects. Finder example is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Other than playing a Zap of some kind, or an effect that specifically allows you to interrupt an action, no. You must complete an effect before executing another one. When two things should happen simultaneously, use the Timing Rules. Keep in mind, a subseqent effect could still undo the original effect.

questions.question: What cards can be played when someone is trying to collect compensation from you (for instance, if someone is trying to collect compensation from you, or if you’ve been Plagued)?
questions.ruling_summary: Cards may be legally played before compensation starts, but hand-targeting effects cannot then be interrupted except by Zaps/explicit interrupts. Hacker's target is too late to dump reinforcements.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Compensation does not create any kind of “lien” or “hold” or “freeze” on your hand. You are free to use any cards that may be legally played before compensation begins to be collected. So, you could play a reinforcement card to get it out of your hand before compensation is taken, for instance. However, once the opportunity to play such cards has passed and compensation begins, then it is too late. For example, you cannot wait to see if Hacker is going to target you before deciding whether to “dump” your reinforcement cards, because the time to affect encounter totals has already passed. Once an effect targets your hand, nothing can interrupt that effect except a Zap or some other power or effect that specifically lets you interrupt it.

questions.question: Can you play reinforcements if one side revealed an attack, but the other side revealed a negotiate, or if both sides revealed negotiates?
questions.ruling_summary: An involved player may play a reinforcement on either side regardless of revealed encounter-card types. See flagged tension with Q032.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, any player involved in the encounter may play a reinforcement on either side, regardless of what type of encounter cards were revealed.

questions.question: Is there a difference between winning an encounter and having a successful encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Winning and making a deal are successful encounters; a deal is not a win for effects such as Cudgel or Barbarian. Guerrilla example excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Winning an encounter counts as having a successful encounter, but so does making a deal. A deal does not count as a “win” for effects that do not explicitly mention deals, such as Cudgel, Barbarian, and Guerrilla.

questions.question: How does Mobius Tubes work if you have no planets?
questions.ruling_summary: Mobius Tubes releases ships; those without a colony return to the warp, except the offense can first place up to four in the gate.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Your ships exit the warp, then any ships that have no colony to return to are returned to the warp. If you are the offense, you may place up to four of your ships in the hyperspace gate before the others are lost to the warp.

questions.question: What is the difference between the Start Turn phase and the Regroup phase?
questions.ruling_summary: Start Turn occurs only on the first encounter, before Regroup effects; offense draws a new hand before a Regroup Plague.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Start Turn is essecntially the first part of the Regroup phase (only occuring on a player’s first encounter as offense), and any effect that happens during Start Turn must take effect before anything that is supposed to happen during Regroup (e.g., the offense draws a new hand before a Plague artifact can be played).

questions.question: What order do cards go into the discard pile? Normally this doesn’t matter, but the Fido flare was in the game, and it calls on forcing a player to draw the top card of the discard pile.
questions.ruling_summary: When order matters, discard non-encounter cards alphabetically/numerically first, then encounter cards from offense clockwise with defense last/top. Expansion Omni-Zap/Cavalry examples excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: When card order matters, non-encounter cards are discarded first, in alphabetical and numerical order, then encounter cards, starting with the offense and going clockwise, and ending with the defense. The defense’s encounter card goes on top of the discard pile. Example: Omni-Zap, Reinforcement +2, Reinforcement +3, offense’s encounter card, Cavalry’s encounter card, defense’s encounter card.

questions.question: Can CE be played with only 2 players?
questions.ruling_summary: The FAQ gives no official two-player variant.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: There is no official 2-player variant for the current edition yet.

questions.question: When you draw your own color from the destiny pile, and you want to automatically establish a colony on your planet, do you go through all of the encounter phases? Do you go through any of them past “Destiny”?
questions.ruling_summary: Automatically reclaiming an empty home planet proceeds only through Launch.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Only through the Launch phase.

questions.question: If you have no ships outside the encounter, can you still invoke effects that require sacrificing a ship from outside the encounter (such as Void Wild flare) by sacrificing one that’s in it?
questions.ruling_summary: A required sacrifice from outside the encounter cannot be paid with an involved ship.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: If you must lose ships that aren’t in the current encounter (such as Grudge), what happens if you have no ships outside the encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: If no ships exist outside the encounter when such losses are required, lose none.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You lose nothing.

questions.question: If you have no ships to place into the hyperspace gate, or your last ship there is removed, what happens?
questions.ruling_summary: An encounter continues with no offensive ships; victory gives no foreign colony unless an effect specifically permits it.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Proceed with the encounter. If the offense wins, they don’t establish a foreign colony unless some effect specifically allows them to do so.

questions.question: Is it allowable to say what is in your hand? The rules explicitly say you can’t show your hand to anyone, but it’s vague on the telling. Can you lie?
questions.ruling_summary: Hand contents may be claimed or lied about, but cards cannot be shown absent an effect; Mind has its own speech restrictions.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You may make whatever ludicrous claims about what you have in your hand, but you cannot SHOW your cards to anyone else (unless a game effect causes you to do so). Note: the Mind has specific restrictions about what can be said.

questions.question: What is the difference between an encounter card’s value, and its identity for all the effects that change values or target certain cards?
questions.ruling_summary: Modified values determine encounter totals; a card's printed identity governs other targeting effects. Morph remains a Morph by identity. Expansion examples excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: An encounter card’s value can change, and whatever it is changed to becomes its new value (e.g., Mirror reversing digits, Tripler dividing a high value into a low one, Warhawk changing negotiates into attack 00). In these cases, the card has a new value. Thus, if Joker’s current wild is an attack 00, the negotiate revealed by Warhawk’s opponent would become wild. Values only matter for encounter totals. A card’s identity is the actual printed value. A Morph’s identity is a morph, no matter what it copies. Any game effect that targets a card outside of encounter totals is targeting its identity. See next three questions.

questions.question: Does a modified card retain its original identity or its modified identity when something else references it (e.g., a Morph of an attack 08 when The Claw has an attack 08 as its claw card)?
questions.ruling_summary: Encounter-resolution effects use the current modified card type/value; other effects use the printed type/value. Expansion-specific The Claw behavior excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Unless otherwise specified, game effects that strictly affect encounter resolution—meaning those effects that impact encounter card types/values, kickers, reinforcements, main player totals, the method of determining the winner and loser, deals, compensation, rewards, and disposition of the involved ships such as landing on the planet, returning to colonies, going to the warp, etc.—all refer to the card’s current, modified type/value. Every other kind of game effect refers to the card’s original, printed type/value. Therefore, The Claw does not activate on the Morph card unless an actual Morph card is the claw. Likewise, if the claw is a 12 and the Mirror causes a 21 to turn into a 12, The Claw does not use its power.

questions.question: Does a Morph count as an attack card if it duplicated an attack card?
questions.ruling_summary: Morph copying an attack is treated as that attack for encounter totals; do not import The Claw.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Once it has duplicated your opponent’s card, it is treated as that card in all ways pertaining to encounter totals (therefore, not for The Claw’s claw card).

questions.question: If a power such as Calculator, Mirror, or Tripler affects a card, does a Morph copy the card’s value before or after the modification?
questions.ruling_summary: Morph copies the initially revealed value, not later changes; it may then be independently modified, as with Tripler.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: The Morph copies whatever value is initially revealed. If that value is later modified, the Morph’s value does not change with it. However, the Morph’s value may be affected by modifications separately.For instance, if the Tripler revealed a Morph and their opponent revealed a 12, the Morph would become a 12 and then get divided to a 4 by Tripler’s power. On the other hand, if Tripler revealed the 12 and their opponent revealed the Morph, the Morph would become a 12, but would not get divided to a 4 just because the card it morphed into did.

questions.question: If a player discards several cards at the same time, are the other players allowed to look at all of them? It is especially useful to have this information before deciding whether to play the Reserve Wild flare or Space Junk artifact.
questions.ruling_summary: Simultaneously discarded faceup cards may all be inspected, absent a contrary power.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, since each card is discarded faceup it is open information unless a power states otherwise.

questions.question: Some powers kick in if one reveals an Attack card (for instance Brute, Cudgel, and Deuce). But what happens if e.g. Cudgel reveals a Negotiate, and then uses the Human Wild flare to turn it into an Attack 42? Can Cudgel then use its power, or not?
questions.ruling_summary: Changing a negotiate into attack 42 with Human Wild does not satisfy Cudgel's requirement of originally revealing an attack. Brute/Deuce excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: No, the originally revealed card is the one considered “revealed.”

questions.question: If you lose your alien power, are you still considered to be that alien?
questions.ruling_summary: A player who loses a power is no longer considered that alien.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Can you play a reinforcement card on a negotiate?
questions.ruling_summary: The FAQ says a reinforcement cannot be played 'on a negotiate'; preserve alongside Q014's permission to play one on either side regardless of card types without imposing an unsupported reconciliation.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: What happens if a player has no colonies or ships on their turn?
questions.ruling_summary: A player with no colonies or ships retrieves one ship at Regroup and may place it on any home planet. This specific FAQ instruction differs from rulebook's general no-colony placement into the gate.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: During the regroup phase, they will retrieve one ship from the warp, and can place it on any of their home planets.

questions.question: Can aliens like Fodder, Porcupine and Reserve use their power multiple times during the reveal phase or must all cards be discarded at once?
questions.ruling_summary: Fodder and Reserve choose all cards for one power use together, rather than repeated selections. Porcupine excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Their power includes one or more cards, all must be chosen at the same time.

questions.question: Does the game end immediately if a player has the required number of foreign colonies, or do you play the encounter through the last phase (Resolution)?
questions.ruling_summary: Ordinary foreign-colony victory waits until the very end of Resolution, allowing prevention effects; explicitly immediate win effects such as Masochist differ.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Unless otherwise specified (e.g. Masochist’s power), the game does not immediately end. Players have until the very end of the Resolution phase to stop a player (or players) from winning the game. See next question.

questions.question: Do effects that let you “immediately win the game” still have to play out until the end of the resolution phase, like the Glutton Wild flare if it is played in Regroup?
questions.ruling_summary: An explicitly immediate win ends the game when its effect resolves unless zapped or explicitly interrupted. The Glutton flare itself is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: No, unless an effect is zapped, or something specifically lets you interrupt the effect, the game ends.

questions.question: What happens if players cannot have an encounter in your system because all of your home planets have been destroyed (Omega Missile, Locust, etc.)?
questions.ruling_summary: If all home planets are destroyed, redraw that player's destiny color. Omega Missile is a base Tech example; Locust excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Players redraw from destiny when your color comes up.

questions.question: What do you do if you have colonies on all of the planets in the defensive system?
questions.ruling_summary: If offense already has colonies on every planet in the defensive system, redraw destiny.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You draw from destiny again.

questions.question: Do you HAVE to retrieve a ship from the warp during regroup?
questions.ruling_summary: Regroup retrieval is mandatory when possible.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Are all discard piles open, public information?
questions.ruling_summary: Discard piles are public unless an effect says otherwise.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, unless otherwise indicated.

questions.question: Can players keep the number of cards in their hand secret?
questions.ruling_summary: Hand size must be disclosed unless an effect allows secrecy.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. If a player wants to know how many cards you have, you must reveal that amount, unless an effect specifcally allows you to keep it secret.

questions.question: Does all table talk have to be public?
questions.ruling_summary: Table talk must be public unless an effect says otherwise.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, unless an effect specifies otherwise.

questions.question: Are defensive allies considered to be “in” the hyperspace gate?
questions.ruling_summary: Defensive allies count as in the hyperspace gate for effect terminology.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: When you are forced to lose, sacrifice, or give another player one of your ships, does it have to be from a colony?
questions.ruling_summary: Unless otherwise specified, forced ship loss/sacrifice/transfer chooses a ship under your control. The researching-Tech example is excluded with the Technology variant.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Unless otherwise indicated, you must choose a ship under your control. That will typically be from a colony, or a researching tech.

questions.question: How do you choose cards “at random” (compensation, Enigma Device, Hate Wild, Mite, Mutant, Mutant Wild, Oracle Wild, Trader Wild, Magician) when both kinds of card backs are involved?
questions.ruling_summary: Random card selection means selecting without seeing faces. Different reward-card backs are an expansion-only example.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Players are allowed to see which card backs they are selecting. In essence, “at random” means “without seeing the faces of the cards.”

questions.question: Can I start a second encounter with no encounter cards with the hope that I can acquire one before the planning phase?
questions.ruling_summary: A second encounter requires an encounter card already in hand as well as a successful first encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. If, on your first encounter, you either win an attack or successfully negotiate, and you have at least one encounter card left in your hand, you may choose to make a second encounter. Otherwise, your turn ends.

questions.question: Do you have to discard a rift, kicker, Retreat, Morph, Intimidate, Variable Attack when someone Plagues you?
questions.ruling_summary: Plague requires one held card of each actual type, including Morph; the extra rift/kicker/retreat/intimidate types and variable attacks are excluded from the original set.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Yes, you must discard one card of each type that you hold. Variable Attack still counts as an attack card, so if you discard a “normal” attack card, you are not also required to discard a Variable Attack. (See “Card Types” in Errata and Clarifications.)

questions.question: What happens if a player has chosen an alien with Do Not Use restrictions on it?
questions.ruling_summary: Remove the alien with the printed incompatibility; its player may use their rejected alien or draw a replacement flare, redrawing conflicts.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: The alien that has the printed restriction is removed from the game, and the one without the restriction remains in play. The affected player may then choose either to use the second alien they were dealt and rejected, or to draw a replacement flare from the unused flare deck and become that alien (redrawing if another conflict arises).

questions.question: Who chooses which ships are lost when an effect causes extra ships to be lost (e.g., Gambler or Skeptic)?
questions.ruling_summary: Absent contrary text, the player losing extra ships chooses which ships. Gambler applies; Skeptic excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Unless an effect specifies otherwise, the player losing the extra ships gets to choose which ships are lost.

questions.question: Are players required to play any applicable cards in hand right before drawing a new hand?
questions.ruling_summary: Before a new hand, playing legal cards is optional; remaining cards must be discarded.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. They may play cards, if appropriate, but all they are required to do is discard whatever cards they were holding.

questions.question: What does “legal encounter” mean?
questions.ruling_summary: A legal encounter can ultimately yield a foreign colony without requiring a deal.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: An encounter where the offense can ultimately gain a foreign colony without necessarily having to make a deal.

questions.question: Are alien powers generally limited to one use per encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Powers are usable once per relevant context unless specified otherwise, e.g. Hate once per turn and Vulch each qualifying artifact discard.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Unless they specifically indicate otherwise (like Hate, which only works oncer per turn, or Vulch, which happens whenever any other player discards an artifact card), an alien’s power is usable once per relevant context.

questions.question: What happens when a planet is captured or moved to another player’s system?
questions.ruling_summary: A moved/captured planet becomes a home planet of its new system. This general rule may matter to Genesis; Pygmy and The Claw special characteristics are excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: That planet is considered a home world for the owner of its new system. For example, if a planet is added to Pygmy’s system, it can only hold up to four ships and counts as half a foreign colony for other players. If a Pygmy planet is captured by The Claw, it counts as a full foreign colony for The Claw.

questions.question: Can a player change their mind about invoking a power or effect if somone else’s action or timing rule outcome changes the game state? As an example, Trader attempts to trade hands with Visionary, but since both aliens use their powers in the same phase, and Visionary is offense, he wishes to use their power first to force Trader to play an attack 04 (knowing Trader will get Visionary’s attack 04 if they trade hands). Can Trader decide to not trade hands at this point?
questions.ruling_summary: A player may reconsider an invoked optional effect if another action/timing changes the state. Trader example generalizes; Visionary excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Where in the Timing Rules do affects not associated with any player fall (for example, the Black Hole hazard)?
questions.ruling_summary: Effects associated with no player resolve after all players in the timing order; the Black Hole hazard itself is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Those are last, after players who are not main players, clockwise from the offense.

questions.question: Do you have to vacate a colony to exchange them in a deal?
questions.ruling_summary: Deal colonies coexist; do not vacate a colony when granting one. Grant only where you currently have a colony, including a foreign colony.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Unless an effect indicates otherwise, your ships coexist with the other player in the deal. You can only give a colony to a player on a planet where you have a colony (even a foreign colony). Vacating the planet would mean you lost that colony.

questions.question: In a deal, do both players have to give something to the other, or can a successful deal be “one-sided”?
questions.ruling_summary: A one-sided deal is valid if at least one card or colony changes hands.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: The deal may be one-sided, however at least 1 colony or card must change hands.

questions.question: Are the terms of a deal EXPLICITLY RESTRICTED to one or more of the following categories: t granting a single colony on a planet you already occupy t giving cards from your hand t specialized use of your power where indicated (such as Zombie’s regeneration)
questions.ruling_summary: Tangible deal terms are limited to permitted cards/one colony and explicit power/card exceptions. At least one card or colony must change hands; promises are allowed but unenforceable.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, the tangible things traded in a deal are explicitly restricted to what’s allowed in the rules (and anything else allowed by a specific power or card), and at least one colony or one card must always change hands for the deal to be valid. Players are free to add non-tangible terms to the deal, such as promises of future actions, but these are unenforceable. See also next question.

questions.question: Can you trade tech cards in a deal?
questions.ruling_summary: Tech cards cannot be traded in a deal.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: If you fail a deal, can you remove ships from a researching tech as part of the three you lose to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Failed-deal ship losses may come from researching Tech.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: During a deal, can you be specifc about what cards you are exchanging, like “I’ll give you a negotiate and an attack 10”? In other words, can you lie?
questions.ruling_summary: Card/colony deal terms may be vague or specific, but cannot be lied about and must be fulfilled.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You may be explicit or vague in the terms of your deal, but you may not lie about what you are offering, and must abide by the terms of your deal with regard to colonies and cards changing hands (e.g., if you say “I will give you my highest attack card,” you must do so if that is part of the deal).

questions.question: After you play a flare, at what point does it re-enter your hand?
questions.ruling_summary: A played flare returns to hand immediately after resolving its effect; Oracle Wild remains outside the mixed hands until then.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Immediately after resolving its effect. So, for instance, when playing the Oracle Wild flare, you play the flare faceup in front of you, mix your hands together, get your new hand at random from the mixed cards, and then return the Oracle flare to your hand (since its effect is now finished).

questions.question: If a flare that can be played at any time changes hands, can it be used a second time in the encounter by the new owner?
questions.ruling_summary: A flare transferred to a new owner cannot be played twice in one encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Any given flare may only be played once per encounter.

questions.question: If you attempt to play a flare but it gets Card Zapped (or for some other reason it is cancelled), does that count against a player’s limit of one flare per encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: A canceled flare counts against the player's one-flare limit if the flare itself was targeted.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes it does count, if the flare itself was targeted.

questions.question: If someone uses a flare that is affected by ship count (such as Virus Wild or Virus Super), do Macron’s ships count as 4 for its purposes?
questions.ruling_summary: When an effect specifies ship number, each Macron ship counts as one, including Virus flares. Fungus excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: When the number of ships is specified, Macron or Fungus’ stack of ships would count as 1 ship each.

questions.question: If your power is zapped and you play your own flare for its Wild effect, and the flare requires you to give it to (your alien) or discard it if your alien is not playing, who do you give the flare to?
questions.ruling_summary: If zapped, use your own flare as Wild and keep it after resolution rather than giving it to yourself/discarding it as if your alien were absent.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You keep the flare after resolving its effects.

questions.question: If you steal another player’s alien sheet and have its flare, do you get to use the Super?
questions.ruling_summary: Stealing another player's alien sheet does not grant use of that alien's Super flare; do not infer new base stealing mechanics.
questions.scope_reason: The stated stolen-alien-sheet scenario requires a sheet-stealing expansion effect; standard original-base rules do not create that scenario. Do not import it as a new base mechanic.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: The Schizoid Wild flare: If Player A achieves the normal victory condition of 5 colonies, is it still possible for Player B to use the Schizoid Wild flare to switch colors with Player A to “steal the win.” Or is the game over once Player A reaches 5 colonies?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No, it is not possible for Player B to steal the win. Only immediate effects can prevent a victory, the Schizoid Wild flare happens “after the end of the encounter.”

questions.question: The Schizoid Wild flare specifies that players swap home systems and colors (and therefore presumably all ships, including foreign colonies, but not hands, racial powers etc.?) - but what happens to ships currently engaged in researching Tech cards, and what about Space Stations?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Techs currently being researched will swap players, as well as Space Stations (they remain attached to whatever planet they were attached to).

questions.question: After an alien power has been Cosmic Zapped, do parts of the power that do not require a use still work or is the alien disabled entirely until the end of this encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Unzappable non-use parts of a power still function after Cosmic Zap; this follows rulebook p12.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Page 12 of the rulebook states: “Some alien powers (or some parts of aliens’ powers) do not require the power to be used. Powers such as these that function without being used cannot be the target of the ‘Cosmic Zap.’”

questions.question: Can you Cosmic Zap a power when that player is using a flare to use their own power (say as an ally when otherwise he can’t use their power as an ally)?
questions.ruling_summary: An actual power use enabled by a Super flare may be Cosmic Zapped.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Some powers have different phases highlighted for use that the Super flare doesn’t correspond to. Can you still zap them?
questions.ruling_summary: Power use remains zappable even when Super changes its usual phase.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: If you Cosmic Zap a player that is using their Super flare, does he discard the flare, or does he have to play the Wild?
questions.ruling_summary: Cosmic Zap of Super-enabled power neither discards the flare nor forces immediate Wild play; it stays in hand and Wild is available while zapped.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Neither. The flare remains in their hand, but he may use the Wild flare while their power is zapped.

questions.question: When exactly can you play a Cosmic Zap?  For example, can you wait to see what card Philanthropist is giving you, or what question Seeker is asking you, or what cards Chosen draws as divine intervention?
questions.ruling_summary: Zap may follow the immediate revealed effect (Chosen draws; Philanthropist's given card), but only in the short same-phase window before later actions; no retroactive Zap after reinforcements change the outcome. Seeker excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Yes, you can wait to see the immediate effect of a power. However, the window of opportunity is relatively short while still in the same phase.  For example, if you choose not to Cosmic Zap Chosen when they draw divine intervention because the added attack card is not enough for Chosen to win (but then after playing reinforcements, Chosen has the higher total), you cannot then play a Cosmic Zap to undo the divine intervention. Once play has moved into the next phase (from Planning to Reveal, for instance), it is too late.

questions.question: Can you preemptively zap a power?
questions.ruling_summary: Cosmic Zap cannot be played preemptively.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: If you are Cosmic Zapped during the Start Turn phase, is your power available in a later phase?
questions.ruling_summary: A Start Turn Zap lasts throughout the current encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Start Turn is still part of the same encounter.

questions.question: Is the intention of the Coldsleep Ship that the new colony must be formed in a system in which the player has no other colonies, or simply that the new colony must be on a planet on which the player has no existing colonies?
questions.ruling_summary: Coldsleep Ship grants a colony on any unoccupied-by-you planet outside your home system; another colony in the same system is allowed.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: The colony is placed on any planet where you do not already have a colony (outside of your own system).

questions.question: Can you research and reveal a tech card at the same time? (So, if the tech needs 2 ships, could you place the second ship on the tech and reveal it in the same regroup phase?)
questions.ruling_summary: Normally research and completion cannot occur in the same Regroup; conditional reveal Tech such as Gluon Mines can be researched and revealed in one encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Unless a tech specifically allows you to, you may not both research and complete a tech in the same encounter phase. However, some techs are only revealed upon certain conditions, such as the Gluon Mines. Such techs may be both researched and revealed during the same encounter.

questions.question: If you have two techs, can you research both of them in the same encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Only one researching ship may be added to one Tech per encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: No, you may only add one ship to any of your techs in a given encounter.

questions.question: If you fail a deal, can you remove ships from a researching tech as part of the three you lose to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Researching ships may pay failed-deal losses.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: What happens to techs if an effect causes a player to switch colors or home systems?
questions.ruling_summary: Researching and completed Tech transfer with a switched color/home system; no new base color-switch effect is implied.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: The techs transfer with the system. So if Red were researching a tech and has two ships on it, and another player takes over Red, they get that researching tech. This counts for completed techs as well, like Lunar Cannon.

questions.question: Are ships researching a tech stuck there until it is done researching?
questions.ruling_summary: Researching ships remain assigned unless an effect removes them; choosing completion with insufficient research abandons/discards the Tech and frees them.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Typically, although an effect that causes you to lose ships of your choice could target researching ships. However, during any regroup, you can choose to complete a tech that has fewer ships than the research number, thereby abandoning it. The tech is then discarded.

questions.question: What happens to your researching ships from the Coldsleep Ship if you have no other colonies?
questions.ruling_summary: If Coldsleep Ship is completed with no other colonies, its researching ships land on the new colony.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: They all get to land on the new colony.

questions.question: Do you have to reveal what card you take from the discard pile when you use the Delta Scanner?
questions.ruling_summary: Delta Scanner retrieval need not be revealed.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: No, you do not need to reveal it.

questions.question: Can the Parasite ally with the defense even if the Energy Cloak is used? (Since the Energy Cloak only stops invitations, not allies themselves.)
questions.ruling_summary: Parasite may join defense despite Energy Cloak stopping invitations.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes, Parasite may ally with the defense.

questions.question: What exactly can the Genesis planet be used for? There’s confusion about how many planets to maintain your power.
questions.ruling_summary: Genesis adds a planet and permits one extra lost home colony before power is disabled; do not replace the rule with a fabricated alternate threshold.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: The Genesis planet is an extra planet that you may place colonies on. This provides you one additional planet that can be lost before your power turns off. (See Errata and Clarifications on page 1.)

questions.question: If the Genesis Bomb is used twice in a game, does the second user simply move the planet to their own system, keeping all previously- placed ships on it?
questions.ruling_summary: A second Genesis Bomb moves the existing Genesis planet and all ships to the new system; the user establishes a colony with researching ships.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes, he then gains a colony on the Genesis planet, placing any of the ships used to research the tech onto the planet.

questions.question: If the Lunar Cannon or Prometheus technologies are completed twice in the same game, what happens to the existing Lunar Cannon or Prometheus tokens?
questions.ruling_summary: Lunar Cannon and Prometheus stay in play; if discarded their tokens leave play, so a later completion places the token normally.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: The Lunar Cannon and Prometheus tech cards remain in play after they are completed. The only way they can be researched a second time is if the tech card is discarded. If that were to happen, then its associated token would be removed from play as well. Therefore, the second player to complete those technologies places the tokens normally.

questions.question: Does the defense choose which ships are lost to Gluon Mines? Can allies be removed from an encounter completely because of them, and are they considered to have allied in the first place?
questions.ruling_summary: Defense selects Gluon Mines losses; an ally removed entirely still counts as having allied.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: The defense chooses which ships are lost, and yes allies can be completely removed. They are still considered to have allied, however.

questions.question: If the Omega Missile destroys a planet, do you still need three home colonies to retain your power?
questions.ruling_summary: Omega Missile does not lower the requirement of three home colonies to keep powers.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: The Precursor Seed says “while this tech is in play you may use the extra alien power...” Does this mean that if you draw an alien with a mandatory power you can treat that power as optional?
questions.ruling_summary: Precursor Seed does not turn a mandatory acquired power into an optional one.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: How many planets must you control to retain use of your second alien acquired with the Precursor Seed?
questions.ruling_summary: Three home colonies retain all Precursor Seed powers, or two with Four Planets.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: You must retain three home planets to retain all of your powers (or two in a four-planet game).

questions.question: Does the Qax have to be re-researched when given, or can it be re-played as soon as the next encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Qax does not need re-research after transfer and may be used the following encounter.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: It does not need to be re-researched, and yes it may be played as soon as the next encounter.

questions.question: If the Qax forces Amoeba to ally, can he then play their Super and escape?
questions.ruling_summary: Amoeba forced to ally by Qax may use Super to escape.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does the Qax force Macron to bring 4 ships?
questions.ruling_summary: Qax does not override Macron's normal one-ship launch restriction.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: No. The Qax does not give the Macron any special ability to bring 4 ships, so Macron’s power works as normal.

questions.question: Can the Tech Scrambler be played at any time someone’s using a tech, or only when the tech is first completed? Does it have to be when the tech is used (analogous to a Tech Zap)?
questions.ruling_summary: Tech Scrambler can cancel any active revealed Tech at any time, not only at completion/use.
questions.scope_reason: Task explicitly excludes optional Technology and other variants. This is an excluded optional rule, not an essential missing-source gap.
questions.source_answer: Tech Scrambler can cancel any active revealed tech at any time.

questions.question: After playing Leviathan Super flare, what happens with allied ships on the worldship when a Force Field artifact is played? Do they have to leave the worldship?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The ships do not leave as the Leviathan Super flare is separate from alliances.

questions.question: Can you play a card in response to a Finder artifact, to prevent the player from finding the card? For example, a flare or a Cosmic Zap (provided playing these cards is appropriate).
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No, except for a Card Zap, to cancel the Finder.

questions.question: When are kickers revealed?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The are revealed in the reveal phase.

questions.question: Does a kicker multiply a card value before or after the effects of card modifying powers such as Calculator, Gaviton, Mirror or Tripler? What about the effects of flares such as Calculator Wild or Gambler Wild?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: After.

questions.question: How does a kicker work with a Crooked Deal negotiate?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The 3 ships lost in a deal or the number of cards taken in compensation is adjusted up or down by 1 first, then multiplied by the kicker. For example, if you had 3 ships and negotiated with a Crooked Deal and a kicker x2 while your opponent played an attack, you would receive 8 cards in compensation (3+1x2).

questions.question: Is either main player required to commit to using or not using a kicker before the other main player decides about kickers?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Either main player may change their mind, but if they cannot ultimately decide, the offense must commit first.

questions.question: If my opponent plays a kicker and I reveal a negotiate, is my compensation increased?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. A kicker only affects the encounter card of the player who played it (unless otherwise indicated). You would only increase your compensation if you had revealed the kicker.

questions.question: As the defense, can you play a kicker before drawing a new hand?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. kickers are played before encounter cards (and announced), and the defense draws a new hand when needing to play an encounter card (after kickers are played).

questions.question: Does any reference to “the deck” or “the discard pile” on any card exclude the reward deck/discard pile?
questions.ruling_summary: Unqualified deck/discard means cosmic deck/discard. Reward deck exceptions themselves are excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: “The deck” always refers to the cosmic deck, and “the discard pile” always refers to the cosmic deck discard pile, unless otherwise stated.

questions.question: Which main player must commit an encounter card when both main players keep switching between cosmic and reward deck cards during planning phase?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: If both players cannot agree, the offense must commit their encounter card first, and then the defense may decide which type of encounter card to play (and the offense can no longer change their mind).

questions.question: Can effects such as Mind Wild flare target the reward deck?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Unless the reward deck is specified, any effect that targets a deck can only be applied to the cosmic deck. The same is true of the discard pile.

questions.question: Do you have to declare how many cards you wish to draw from the reward deck when taking rewards, or can you take one to see how good it is before deciding to take the rest from the cosmic deck?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: You must declare all of your reward sources before taking them. That is, you must state “I will take one ship from the warp, one card from the cosmic deck, and two from the reward deck” if receiving four rewards, for example.

questions.question: Are players ever allowed to hide the design of a card back from other players?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Is it correct to say that the term “discard” now means “discard to whichever discard pile is appropriate based on the card back,” but only in the context of putting cards into a discard pile, not taking them out?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes, except for effects that take cards out immediately after discarding (see below).

questions.question: What happens with effects that change the destination of a discarded card before it is discarded? For example, Mite Super flare says you “take any cards your opponent discards” Can Mite intercept only non- reward-deck cards?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Effects that intercept cards on their way to the discard pile, or that grab cards that were just discarded, can affect cards going/just gone to the reward deck discard pile. Things that happen later cannot retrieve cards from that pile, but there is a small window of opportunity after the cards are freshly discarded where they may be immediately retrieved.

questions.question: How do you choose cards “at random” when both cosmic and reward cards are involved?
questions.ruling_summary: Random card selection forbids looking at faces; reward-card mixing is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Players are allowed to see which card backs they are selecting. In essence,”at random” means “without seeing the faces of the cards.”

questions.question: I don’t understand rifts, when do they go off?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Rifts go off when a player takes a rift from another player. However, if a player is given a rift, it does not go off. For example, when the Trader trades their hand with another player, and he receives a rift, the effect would occur because he took the cards. However, if the player he traded with received a rift into their hand, the effect would not occur, because that player was given the card. An easier way to think of it is like this: If a player is thieving a rift, it will go off.

questions.question: When Trader takes another player’s hand, do the rifts in it detonate?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes, since Trader is taking the rifts. Any rifts in the hand Trader is giving to the other player do not detonate (since the other player is not taking them).

questions.question: Is a rift triggered when Philanthropist gives one to another player?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. In this case, the card was given, not taken.

questions.question: Are rifts triggered when Barbarian pillages another player’s hand?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Only if Barbarian takes one of the rifts. Typically, Barbarian will discard those cards after pillaging a hand, so the rift never entered Barbarian’s hand.

questions.question: If you use a rift to free another player’s ships from the warp, who gets to decide which colonies they return to?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The owner of the ships.

questions.question: If someone plays the Oracle Wild flare and mixes hands with a player holding a rift, does it detonate if the other player ends up with it after hands have been randomly reassigned?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Can you trade rifts in a deal without detonating them?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: When exactly is a hazard card drawn?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Immediately after revealing a destiny card with the hazard symbol.

questions.question: Is Temporal Anomaly a permanent effect? Does it affect other orders (such as the order in which alliances are chosen?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Temporal Anomaly lasts until another affect changes the order of play. It only affects turn order.

questions.question: The Meteor Storm hazard. The card says that the combined totals for the encounter must exceed 25. Is this intended to be the full totals, as worded, or just the total of the attack cards? This seems clear, but it does seem to be asked quite frequently when players come across this card for the first time, so clarification might be useful.
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The total of cards and ships as normal.

questions.question: The Entropy Beast’s wording is confusing. Should it be taken that as long as the Beast is in play, any time a player is reduced below three home planets as a result of any other game effect (for example the Omega Missile, etc.), all players lose?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No matter what causes it you will lose.

questions.question: Does the Black Hole hazard cause Zombie’s ships lost in an encounter to be removed from the game?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Does The Cosmic Guardian affect attack cards whose value has been modified to 20 or higher, like by the Mirror?

questions.question: Are ships released from a Fungus stack in the warp eligible to be healed by Healer?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: If Fungus wins an encounter with a stack, can they add more losing ships to that same stack?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.

questions.question: Does Fungus capture ships selected by Bully as an ally?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Since the ships Bully selects are the losing ships, those are one that adhere to Fungus.

questions.question: Would Fungus capture the extra ships smashed by Cudgel, or lost due to Grudge or Gambler?

questions.source_answer: Yes to Cudgel, since the additional ships are lost as a result of the encounter (Cudgel simply increases their number). questions.question: Does Fungus receive compensation or rewards for each ship in a stack?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. Each stack counts as one ship for purposes of compensation or rewards.

questions.question: Is it possible for Fungus to reduce a player to fewer than 5 ships?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Do captured ships immediately regain their characteristics upon entering the warp (e.g., Zombie)?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Zombie ships would return to colonies, Fury would gain a token, etc.

questions.question: If you use the Fungus Wild flare, and capture one of Fungus’ stacks, does it count as only one ship, and is the stack freed when the flare is discarded?

questions.question: If Fungus is allied with Anti-Matter and has a ship with 5 other ships stacked under it, does Fungus subtract 6?

questions.question: If Spiff tries to crash-land against Fungus, are all of their ships captured first?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. One ship crash-lands, and the others are captured.

questions.question: Why does Gambler say “Do not use with Sorcerer”?

questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Because it’s not much of a bluff if Sorcerer has already seen the card. If this doesn’t bother you, feel free to go ahead and use them together.

questions.question: How does Gambler interact with Oracle since one forces reveal and one refuses to reveal?
questions.ruling_summary: Gambler must reveal or bluff before Oracle chooses a card.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Gambler must either reveal their card or bluff before Oracle chooses an encounter card.

questions.question: Does Gambler place an unrevealed reward deck encounter card on the bottom of the reward deck?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does Ghoul get to feast on ships that are captured, or eradicated by Void?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. Only ships that are sent to the warp.

questions.question: Does Ghoul feast on ships lost through means other than the normal loss of an encounter (e.g., Cudgel Wild flare, Plague artifact, etc.)?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Only ships lost as a result of losing the encounter.  The Cudgel Wild flare is a separate effect. Plague precedes the encounter.

questions.question: Does Ionic Gas stop Ghoul from using its power?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does Ghoul get to draw from the reward deck when using its power?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does Glutton’s power of retriving “up to” two extra ships from the warp mean that Glutton can retrieve one or none?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. It only refers to when there are fewer of Glutton’s ships available to be retrieved.

questions.question: If Gravitron changes a negative attack card, is the ones or tens digit value of the card still negative?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Is an attack card using only one of the digits still considered to have a 0 in front of it for effects like Mirror?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Do players have the choice of choosing to keep their petrified ships where they are for effects like failed deal in order to not lose any ships to the warp?

questions.source_answer: No. Petrified ships, if chosen for effects that send them to the warp, have them captured, or removed from the game do not get to remain on the planet.

questions.question: If you send ships to ally with Grudge but then they leave the encounter (due to Amoeba’s power or Force Field, for instance), are you then affected by Grudge?
questions.ruling_summary: An ally initially committing at least one ship to Grudge avoids its token even if ships later leave, including through Amoeba or Force Field.
