questions.source_answer: No, as long as you initially ally with at least one ship, you do not receive a grudge token.

questions.question: After Guerrilla loses to Leviathan and uses its power of Attrition, Leviathan will have only one ship left on the worldship. Can this ship still land on Guerrilla’s planet?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. However, if Leviathan has three or fewer ships on its worldship and Guerrilla plays Guerrilla Super flare to send them all to the warp, then Leviathan has nothing to land on the targeted planet. In either case, the worldship returns (empty) to Leviathan’s system and Leviathan has still won the encounter.

questions.question: Do effects like collecting rewards or Cudgel’s power occur before Guerrilla’s power or after?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: They occur after. See Clarifications and Errata.

questions.question: Does Guerrilla Wild have to be used in a player’s home system, and what happens to bystanders on the destroyed planet?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes, it is a home planet belonging to the player with the flare. Bystanders on the planet go to the warp.

questions.question: Can Hacker wait to take compensation from a player that is going to draw rewards from the reward deck?
questions.ruling_summary: Hacker compensation follows offense, defense, then non-main players clockwise. Reward-deck draw source itself is excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Follow the timing rules: 1. The offense. 2. The defense. 3. Players who are not the main players, clockwise from the offense.

questions.question: Can Hate discard a Morph card when using their power? If so, does that mean no one else can discard one, or that whatever they discard will be the same as the Morph?
questions.ruling_summary: Hate can discard Morph, forcing others to discard Morph or lose ships. Special Crooked Deal cards are excluded.
questions.scope_reason: Apply only the base/general ruling summarized below; expansion examples or mechanics in the same entry are excluded.
questions.source_answer: Yes. If Hate discards a Morph card, then everyone else must discard a Morph card or lose ships. Negotiate and Negotiate (Crooked Deal) cards both have the card type of negotiate, so if Hate discards either one, the other players can discard either one.

questions.question: Does Hate have to be zapped before he chooses which card to discard?
questions.ruling_summary: Hate can be Zapped after choosing its discard and then keeps that card.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. If he is zapped after choosing a card to discard, he keeps that card instead.

questions.question: When playing Hate, and you need a new hand on offense, do you get the new hand, then have to hate, or do you lose the opportunity to hate?
questions.ruling_summary: Offensive Hate draws a necessary new hand before using its power.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You draw a new hand, then use your alien power.

questions.question: If Hate discards an attack 20, and all I have is an attack 04, do I get to discard it, even though I still lose ships?
questions.ruling_summary: Against Hate's attack 20, a player without a higher attack they wish to discard discards nothing and loses three ships; a lower attack cannot be discarded.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. If you do not have an attack card higher than 20 you wish to discard, then you discard nothing and lose three ships.

questions.question: If Healer heals someone, are their ships removed from the warp or stopped from going to the warp? (Asked because, if ships are sent to the warp and then healed, Remora could cling and get ships every time Healer heals.)
questions.ruling_summary: Healer returns ships after they have actually reached the warp, permitting Remora retrieval triggers.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: The ships go to the warp and then are returned from the warp.

questions.question: Can Healer use their power before Zombie evades going to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Healer cannot heal Zombie ships prevented from reaching the warp.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No, because the Zombie’s power kicks in before he goes to the warp at all.

questions.question: If Healer heals Vacuum, does Vacuum still get to use their power?
questions.ruling_summary: Vacuum triggers on actual warp loss before healing; Healer can then heal Vacuum's and other eligible non-Healer ships.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Vacuum’s ships go to the warp first, and thus can take others along. Healer may then heal those ships as well, if they are not Healer’s.

questions.question: Are ships released from a Fungus stack in the warp eligible to be healed by Healer?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does Horde add a horde token when drawing from the reward deck, the destiny deck, the tech deck, etc.?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. Just from the cosmic deck.

questions.question: Does Human’s zap-him-to-win beat Pacifist’s play-an-N-to-win?
questions.ruling_summary: Human/Pacifist conflicting wins resolve by normal timing: the first effect wins.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Whichever effect goes off first wins. Use the standard timing rules to determine which effect goes off first.

questions.question: Can Human be zapped to win even if one or both players reveal a Negotiate card?
questions.ruling_summary: Human can be zapped to win even with one or both negotiates revealed.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: If Human is zapped to win and the opponent revealed a Negotiate card, does the opponent receive compensation?
questions.ruling_summary: Human's opponent gets compensation after Human's zap win only if Human actually revealed an attack.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Only if Human actually revealed an Attack card.

questions.question: How does the Human Super flare work?
questions.ruling_summary: Human Super can add eight and then be discarded to zap, or be discarded solely for zap without adding eight.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Human may play it to add 8 instead of 4. Once played, Human has the option of discarding the flare to zap their power. Alternatively, Human may forego adding 8 and simply discard the flare for its zapping effect.

questions.question: If Industrialist is facing Loser, and Loser has declared an upset, does allowing Industrialist to win the encounter mean that Industrialist actually loses the encounter?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.

questions.question: What is to be done when turning over the Invader’s destiny cards if the Invader has lost their power? Are they skipped and redrawn?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes, they are skipped and a new destiny card is drawn.

questions.question: Does the Invader’s “extra encounter” include all phases of an encounter (including Regroup, but presumably not Destiny), or is the intention that the Invader “takes over” from the current player’s encounter?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The encounter starts from the Launch phase. A regroup/destiny phase is not repeated. Once complete. the original player draws a new destiny card and continues their encounter from that point.

questions.question: If Invader has lost power, what do you do when drawing an “Invasion!” destiny card?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Ignore it and draw again.

questions.question: When another player draws an “Invasion!” destiny, do they get another regroup when they “receive another encounter”?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Is a player that had their first encounter interrupted by an “Invasion!” destiny card still entitled to a second encounter if they win that first one?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: If a player was about to have a second encounter when they revealed an “Invasion!” destiny card, and runs out of encounter cards during Invader’s interrupting encounter, does that player still get to have a second encounter?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: When you draw an Invasion! card and become the defense, does Invader skip over any phases?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. The encounter starts immediately after the Destiny Phase, so Invader does not get a Regroup Phase.

questions.question: Can Kamikaze use its power multiple times during the planning phase to sacrifice one ship at a time or must all ships be sacrificed at once before drawing any cards?
questions.ruling_summary: Kamikaze chooses and sacrifices all ships for one power use together before drawing cards.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: All ships must be sacrificed at once.

questions.question: The Kamikaze Super flare says it works “during each of your regroup phases.” Do you have to play it each time you want to use it, or is it automatic?
questions.ruling_summary: Kamikaze Super must be played anew for each encounter it is used.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You must play the flare each time you want to use its effect.

questions.question: Does Laser get to affect Miser’s hoard?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Do cards set aside by Laser still count as part of your hand?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Does Leviathan bring a planet/worldship in addition to the normal 1-4 launched ships?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The worldship replaces the normal launch. The only other ships you may bring are those already on the worldship.

questions.question: If Guerrilla loses to Leviathan attacking with a worldship that has only 1 ship on it, does that ship get to land on the defensive planet?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.

questions.question: If Leviathan’s power is stolen after a worldship has been placed on the hyperspace gate, does the worldship remain, and if so, does it still count as +20?

However, if the worldship is on the winning side, the controlling player decides how many ships on it get to land on the defensive planet, if any. The worldship then returns to the home system of Leviathan, not the player who has stolen the power.

questions.question: After the Leviathan Wild flare is played, do the swapped planets now count as home colonies in their respective systems?

questions.source_answer: Yes. If Blue’s planet is now in Purple’s system (and vice versa), the Blue planet now counts as a home planet for Purple (and if Purple has ships on it, they are now a home colony).

questions.question: Can Lightning have an extra encounter with no encounter cards in hand (i.e., do they draw a new hand)?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: If Sniveler whines about having fewest foreign colonies, do Locust’s devoured planets count, and if any player refuses to give Sniveler a foreign colony, what happens to Locust’s devoured planet?

questions.source_answer: The devoured planets do count to the total of foreign colonies for Sniveler’s whining. If any player refuses to give Sniveler a colony, Locust’s devoured planets are unaffected (though Locust could still lose a normal foreign colony if they have one).

questions.question: Can Loser declare an upset if Seeker has asked “Are you playing a negotiate?” and Loser answers yes (though still holds an attack card)?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.

questions.question: If Loser calls an upset, does Deuce’s second card have to be an attack card?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.

questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The win here must be the ultimate outcome of the encounter. That is, it doesn’t matter if Loser has declared an upset or not; Industrials must be allowed to win the encounter overall or else Industrialist adds the attack card to the stack.

questions.question: Can I play Loser Wild after my opponent plays a kicker? If so, is the kicker discarded?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Kickers are played before encounter cards are selected, and so is Loser Wild, so yes you can play the flare. However, the kicker returns to your opponent’s hand.

questions.question: When gaining rewards per the Lunatic Wild flare, is the reward deck eligible?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. The player may retrieve ships and draw from either the cosmic deck or the reward deck, or a combination of both (but does not draw the full amount from both decks).

questions.question: Should the Lunatic use an Alliance Dial when allying against themselves?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Does the Machine Wild flare mean you draw 8 new cards and keep the rest of your hand, or must you discard the Machine flare after you play it?

questions.question: The Machine Super flare says it works “during each of your regroup phases.” Do you have to play it each time you want to use it, or is it automatic?

questions.question: The Machine Wild flare says “you may always have a second encounter.” Do you have to play it each time you want to use it, or is it automatic?
questions.ruling_summary: Machine Wild must be played each time its second-encounter effect is desired.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You must play the flare each time you want to use its effect.

questions.question: When can you zap Macron? His power is used to bring only 1 ship in the gate, so is it then, or during resolution?
questions.ruling_summary: Macron can be zapped at launch to allow up to four ordinary ships, or after reveal to remove its four-per-ship value.

questions.source_answer: Macron’s power may be zapped either when launching ships (to launch up to four ships worth 1 each) or after cards are revealed (to keep their ships from being worth 4 each). Macron’s ability has been reworded in the errata section to clarify this intent.

questions.question: Does the Macron Super flare mean to exclude being a defensive ally? The card specifies “launch up to four ships in the hyperspace gate.”
questions.ruling_summary: Macron Super's up-to-four ships also applies when defending as an ally.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Macron Super may launch up to four ships as a defensive ally as well. See errata for timing indicator on this flare card.

questions.question: If Deuce only has two encounter cards, does Magician have any effect?

questions.source_answer: Magician forces Deuce to play two encounter cards (before encounter cards are selected). At that point, Deuce has selected an encounter card, but Deuce’s power kicks in “after cards are selected,” and would either end their turn as offense, or as the defense, draw a new hand, and then play a second card normally.

questions.question: The Masochist Super flare says it works “during each of your regroup phases.” Do you have to play it each time you want to use it, or is it automatic?
questions.ruling_summary: Masochist Super must be played anew each encounter it is used.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: You must play the flare each time you want to use its effect.

questions.question: Does Ionic Gas stop Mercenary from using their power?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: The Merchant’s card specifies that the additional hired ships (cards) they can field can be lost as normal during the encounter, but return to the player’s hand at the end of the encounter. One time this is key is if using these ships to invade a planet with a Saboteur bomb: if the cards return after the encounter, then they would “land” on the planet and be destroyed; but if they are intended to return to the Merchant’s hand as soon as the combat is over, then they are not affected by the bomb.
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: In this case, returning the merchants cards to your hand is the very last thing that happens in the encounter. They are treated as ships; therefore, they would go to the warp in the situation you presented, and thus be discarded.

questions.question: Can hired ships be taken as compensation?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No. They do not return to hand until the end of the encounter.

questions.question: What happens if a hired ship is captured?

questions.ruling_summary: Defensive Trader with no cards must draw a new hand before trading; it cannot trade an empty hand.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Trader must have a hand in order to trade hands. After drawing a new hand, Trader may then choose to trade hands.

questions.question: When Trader takes another player’s hand, do the rifts in it detonate?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes, since Trader is taking the rifts. Any rifts in the hand Trader is giving to the other player do not detonate (since the other player is not taking them).

questions.question: Can Vacuum use its power on itself, and if so, can it cause an infinite loop?
questions.ruling_summary: Vacuum cannot target itself.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Vacuum cannot use its power on itself. See Errata and Clarifications on page 1.

questions.question: Can the Vacuum, with their Super flare, remove a Zombie colony? If Zombie has 4 foreign colonies with 1 ship each, and vacuum loses 4 ships, can the Super remove all 4 of those colonies?
questions.ruling_summary: Vacuum Super losses are simultaneous and can remove all one-ship Zombie foreign colonies; Zombie cannot move saved ships to another colony being lost in that effect.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, and yes. All losses that occur because of a single effect (such as Vacuum Super flare) happen at the same instant, so Zombie could not save one of their ships and send it to another colony that he is losing at the same moment.

questions.question: If Healer heals Vacuum, does Vacuum still get to use their power?
questions.ruling_summary: Vacuum's warp loss triggers before healing; Healer may heal it and other affected non-Healer ships afterward.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Vacuum’s ships go to the warp first, and thus can take others along. Healer may then heal those ships as well, if they are not Healer’s.

questions.question: If you play the Virus Wild flare and have no allies, are you essentially multiplying by zero?
questions.ruling_summary: Virus Wild with no allies multiplies by zero.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Can Visionary specify a Crooked Deal negotiate must be played?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes. But if a player does not have one but does have a regular negotiate, they are not required to play it. Also, if Visionary specifies a negotiate card, and the player only has a Crooded Deal negotiate, it must be played.

questions.question: If you fail to deal with Void, are your ships eradicated?
questions.ruling_summary: Void does not eradicate failed-deal losses; it must win as main player, or as ally with Super.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Void only eradicates when winning as a main player (or ally, when using the Void Super flare).

questions.question: Do you actually get compensation when losing with a negotiate to Void?
questions.ruling_summary: Losing a negotiate to Void yields no compensation because ships never go to the warp.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No.

questions.question: Is there an official ruling on Zombie vs. Void?
questions.ruling_summary: Void eradication precedes/precludes Zombie prevention and Observer protection.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Void trumps Zombie. Zombie’s power kicks in when it should go to the warp, however the intent for Void is that it never sends its opponent’s to the warp at all. Void also trumps Observer.

questions.question: If Vulch gets Cosmic Zapped, does he get the Zap that zapped him?
questions.ruling_summary: Vulch cannot collect the Cosmic Zap that zapped it because the power is unavailable when the Zap is discarded.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No, as he will not have a power when that artifact would go to the discard pile.

questions.question: Can Vulch take discarded artifacts that originated from the reward deck?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Yes.

questions.question: Can Vulch pick up artifacts that are being discarded by a player that has played the Vulch Wild flare against the Vulch?
questions.ruling_summary: Vulch can take artifacts discarded by the player using Vulch Wild against it, potentially handing them back repeatedly.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes. Vulch may then have to hand the artifacts to the player again, who in turn may discard them again, etc.

questions.question: Does the Vulch Super flare mean that Vulch can take all flare cards discarded at the same time, or in the encounter?
questions.ruling_summary: Vulch Super lasts for all eligible flare discards in the encounter; play on the first such discard. It cannot retrieve itself.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: All flares in the encounter. The flare should be played the first time any flares are discarded in the encounter, and then its effect lasts until the end of the encounter, letting Vulch “use” their power any number of times flares are discarded. However, Vulch would not be able to pick up their own flare in this manner.

questions.question: Can you force Warhawk into negotiation by playing an Emotion Control artifact?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Both effects create a timing conflict. Use the timing conflict chart to determine whether warhawk’s ability happens before or after the artifact. In which case the answer would be yes if Warhawk is the offense, and the defense played the artifact.

questions.question: What happens when Warhawk faces off against Bleeding Heart or The Cult?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: The encounter cards ultimately end on a value of Attack 00.

questions.question: If ships are sent to the warp during Reveal, does Warpish update their total accordingly?
questions.ruling_summary: Warpish counts ships added to the warp before its use, not afterward; apply timing rules if needed.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: If the ships are added to the warp prior to Warpish using their power, then yes. If not, then no. Refer to the timing rules if in doubt.

questions.question: If Warrior gets zapped, does he still earn experience?
questions.ruling_summary: Warrior continues earning experience when Zapped because that part does not require power use.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes. See Clarifications and Errata on page 1.

questions.question: If Warrior draws their own color and reclaims an empty home planet, does he collect experience?
questions.ruling_summary: Warrior earns experience for reclaiming an empty home planet, which counts as a win.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, recolonizing a home planet counts as winning an encounter, and Warrior collects experience accordingly.

questions.question: If the defensive main player uses the Whirligig Wild flare and ends up losing their last encounter card, does the flare get added back to the hand before or after drawing a new hand?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: Before. Thus, the flare would be discarded.

questions.question: Can Will attack Blue on Red’s planet even if Blue has no colony there?
questions.ruling_summary: Will cannot attack an absent colony on a third player's planet; a home owner can still defend an empty home planet.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Blue doesn’t have a colony there to attack, while Red may always be forced to defend their home planet.

questions.question: Does the Winner Super flare mean that Winner would get three free colonies if they won by 29 points?
questions.scope_reason: Requires expansion alien/card/module; mentioning a base alien does not bring that expansion interaction into the original CE01 scope.
questions.source_answer: No, only two colonies. The Super effect works in place of, not in addition to, Winner’s base power effect.

questions.question: Does the Zombie get compensation?
questions.ruling_summary: Zombie gets compensation only if its ships actually reach the warp, e.g. while zapped; its ordinary prevention yields none.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Not unless their ships actually go to the warp (such as when their power is Cosmic Zapped). Compensation is awarded based on ships going to the warp, after all. If Zombie’s ships went to the warp and were then retrieved by their power, he would receive compensation, but Zombie’s power prevents them from going to the warp in the first place.

questions.question: Is there a limit to how many ships Zombie can liberate at once as part of a deal?
questions.ruling_summary: Zombie deal liberation has no numerical limit.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No, there is no limit.

questions.question: Can Healer use their power before Zombie evades going to the warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Healer cannot heal Zombie ships that never reach the warp.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No, because the Zombie’s power kicks in before he goes to the warp at all.

questions.question: Can Zombie use the Kamikaze Wild or similar cards that require sending ships to warp to use, and if so, are the ships actually sent to warp?
questions.ruling_summary: Zombie can invoke Kamikaze Wild and similar ship-to-warp costs, then use its power to prevent arrival.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, Zombie may use the card, and then may use their power to prevent those ships from entering the warp.

questions.question: Can the Vacuum, with their Super flare, remove a Zombie colony? If Zombie has 4 foreign colonies with 1 ship each, and vacuum loses 4 ships, can the Super remove all 4 of those colonies?
questions.ruling_summary: Vacuum Super removes simultaneous Zombie colonies without letting saved ships relocate to another colony lost in the same effect.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Yes, and yes. All losses that occur because of a single effect (such as Vacuum Super flare) happen at the same instant, so Zombie could not save one of their ships and send it to another colony that he is losing at the same moment.

questions.question: Is there an official ruling on Zombie vs. Void?
questions.ruling_summary: Void eradicates Zombie's ships directly without sending them to the warp.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: Void trumps Zombie. Zombie’s power kicks in when it should go to the warp, however the intent for Void is that it never sends its opponent’s to the warp at all.

questions.question: Can Zombie free Masochist’s ships when Zombie is making a deal with a different alien (like Void, for instance)?
questions.ruling_summary: Zombie may free only its negotiating opponent's ships in the deal, not third-party Masochist's ships.
questions.scope_reason: Original base rule, base card, original alien, or base Technology variant ruling.
questions.source_answer: No. Zombie could only free Void’s ships in that deal.

errata.heading: Card Types
errata.ruling_summary: Original base card types are attack, negotiate, morph, artifact, flare and reinforcement; encounter is not a card type. The 2018 list also includes expansion-only retreat, intimidate, kicker and rift, which must be excluded.
errata.scope_reason: Base ruling; omit expansion card types.
errata.source_text: As of COSMIC EONS, the following lists all card types for effects like Hate’s power or the Plague artifact: attack, negotiate, morph, retreat, artifact, flare, intimidate, kicker, reinforcement, rift. Note that “encounter” is not a card type.

errata.heading: Cosmic Conflict
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Early printings of COSMIC CONFLICT listed 29 Hazard cards in the components list. There are 28.

errata.heading: Bandit Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Bandit should read “cosmic deck” instead of “encounter deck.”

errata.heading: Changeling Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Changeling’s second sentence should read “Either draw a card from the deck and add it to your hand or swap alien sheets with your opponent.” This clarifies that Changeling is not just using the power, but actually trading sheets. Changeling should read “Warrior’s tokens” rather than “Warrior’s points.”

errata.heading: Chrysalis Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Chrysalis should read “At the start of any encounter, use this power to discard one token from this sheet. If there are no tokens left on this sheet, look at the top 10 flares of the unused flare deck. Choose one of these 10 flares corresponding to an alien that does not have Game Setup text and is allowed in the current game. You become that alien for the rest of the game. Add its flare card to your hand and take its alien sheet. Then, remove the other nine flare cards from the game and return this sheet to the game box.” This clarifies that the 9 flares are not added to the cosmic deck discard pile.

errata.heading: The Claw Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The Claw should read “At the start of any regroup phase, you may swap a non-negotiate card from your hand with your claw.” The claw card can never be a negotiate (of any kind). The third paragraph should read “Once per encounter, when another player plays a card faceup or reveals a copy of the card you have chosen as your claw, use this power and reveal your claw…” This means that cards played faceup will activate the claw, as well as cards that are revealed (even if they weren’t originally played by the same player, as in the case of Sorcerer switching cards).

errata.heading: Crusher Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last sentence of the alien power description should read “If this sheet is lost or turned facedown, all crushed ships are released wherever they are.”

errata.heading: Extortionist Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Extortionist’s first sentence should read “After starting hands are dealt, whenever any other player acquires cards as compensation or draws new cards into their hand…” This clarifies that only cards drawn into hands activate Extortionist’s power, and not drawing from destiny, the Tech deck, etc.

errata.heading: Fire Dancer Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last sentence of the alien power description should “If this {power} sheet is lost or turned facedown, all of your fires are extinguished.”

errata.heading: Graviton Flare
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The Super should have a Planning icon, not Resolution.

errata.heading: Guerrilla Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Guerrilla should read “You have the power of Attrition. As a main player, immediately after you lose an encounter, use this power to weaken your opponent and each of their allies. Each player you weaken loses all but one of their ships in the encounter to the warp. This effect takes place before other resolution effects such as Cudgel’s power or collecting rewards.” This clarifies that Guerrilla alters the number of ships their opponent has when calculating how many rewards they collect, or other effects based on the number of ships an opponent had in the encounter.

errata.heading: Horde Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Horde should read “Each time you draw a card from the cosmic deck…” This prevents Horde from adding a horde token each time they draw from destiny, the Tech deck, etc.

errata.heading: Industrialist Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The sheet should have a Reveal icon, not Resolution.

errata.heading: Love Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The third sentence should read “Each other player, in clockwise order, may then choose and discard one card from their hand.” This removes an errant comma from the original wording, and clarifies that all other players may discard a card.

errata.heading: Lunatic Flare
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The Wild effect shoud read “For each reward you receive, you may both draw a card and retrieve a ship from the warp.” This clarifies that Lunatic may indeed draw from the reward deck.

errata.heading: Poison Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The timing bar should read As Any Player, and Varies (instead of Mandatory).

errata.heading: Pretender Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The first sentence of the alien power description should start with “Once per turn, as the offense, after destiny is drawn, you may use this power to take your alien sheet(s) and everything on them and move to what you consider to be the best seat.” This clarifies that Pretender can only be used once per turn.

errata.heading: Siren Alien Power (CC)
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: Siren’s second paragraph should read “Any time you win an encounter as the defense after using your power, you immediately gain a free foreign colony in the offense’s home system on a planet of your choice.” This clarifies that the “passive” effect of Siren’s power only happens if Siren has used its power (see next correction). Siren’s timing strip should read “Not Offense,” rather than “Not Defense” in its player prerequisite. This clarifies that Siren can use its power when its system comes up in destiny.

errata.heading: Skeptic Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last sentence of the power description should read “If either side loses or a deal fails…” This clarifies that if both sides lose the encounter (e.g., a Morph vs Morph), then both sides lose double.

errata.heading: Surgeon Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The power description should read “after destiny is determined” rather than “after destiny is drawn” to clarify that Surgeon only uses its power once per encounter.

errata.heading: Vacuum Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Original base alien.
errata.source_text: The Vacuum can not target itself with its power.

errata.heading: Warhawk Alien Power
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The end of the alien power description should include: “If an effect creates an infiite loop, the revealed cards are considered to be attack 00s.”

errata.heading: Will Alien Power
errata.ruling_summary: Will must target an actual colony outside the defender's own home system; a home owner may defend an empty planet. Correct Will timing to Destiny, not Launch.
errata.scope_reason: Original base alien.
errata.source_text: When using their power, Will must encounter a colony unless they are encountering a player in their home system. Thus, if Will wishes to encounter Blue on Red’s planet, then Blue must have at least one ship there. Will’s timing strip should read “Destiny” rather than “Launch.”

errata.heading: Butler Flare (CA)
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last line of the Wild flare should read “If that player wins or deals, it counts as a successful encounter for you. Otherwise it counts as being unsuccessful.” This clarifies that whoever played Butler Wild doesn’t resume play at their own same Regroup Phase.

errata.heading: Sadist Flare (CC)
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The Sadist Wild flare should say “Whenever you send another player’s ships to the warp by playing a card or being the main player on the winning side of an encounter, you may draw one card from the deck for each player who lost ships to you.”

errata.heading: Skeptic Flare
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The Super should read “When you tell a player you doubt that they will win, you also tell them how many ships not in the encounter (1-20) are at risk (instead of your normal doubling). If they double- doubt you, instead of doubling their losses the penalized player(s) loses that number of additional ships.” This clarifies that if Skeptic is an ally using this flare, the main player on their side does not lose extra ships; only Skeptic if their side loses.

errata.heading: Sycophant Flare
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last line of the Super should read “Afterwards, give this flare to any other player.” This clarifies that Sycophant can’t give the flare to themself.

errata.heading: Symbiote Flare
errata.scope_reason: Expansion component/alien; excluded even when base aliens are mentioned.
errata.source_text: The last two lines of the Super should read “Your ships coexist with any ships already there. This flare may not be canceled through any means.” This clarifies that the flare effect does not supercede Filth’s power.

source_tensions.detail: p3 L253–257 explicitly permits reinforcements on either side whatever card types were revealed; p4 L374–375 says No to playing a reinforcement on a negotiate. Both occur in the PDF. Wording may distinguish the side from the negotiate itself, but the source does not expressly explain that distinction; preserve ambiguity instead of claiming a definitive restriction.

FAQ p4 L376–379 specifically lets a player with no colonies or ships put the retrieved ship on any home planet, whereas rulebook p7 generally puts a no-colony Regroup ship in the gate. Preserve the specific FAQ exception; do not invent a missing source.

Some FAQ answers refer to errata on p1 that is absent from this 2018 FAQ (Macron rewording/flare icon, Reincarnator timing, Warrior experience, Genesis threshold). The answers themselves still supply the listed ruling. Original component faces remain necessary for other effect details; do not claim those stated rulings are unsupported.

component_authority_limits.detail: The complete 2008 rulebook explains alien-sheet fields and general power rules, but does not print the complete text of all 50 alien powers. The FAQ gives selected changes/interactions rather than replacement sheets. Exact mandatory/optional flags, uses, target limits, phases, setup holdings, restrictions and alternate-win conditions therefore require the corresponding original sheet unless expressly supplied in these sources. The preflight manifest locates all fifty original sheet images; this reviewer used it only to determine membership and did not verify image faces. This is a task handoff to component authority, not a claim that the available project lacks original sheets.

The rulebook supplies complete general flare constraints and a Clone/classic-Filch illustration, while FAQ specifies many particular effects. Exact unquoted Wild/Super effects and timing for each of the original fifty flares require original card faces. Do not infer them from alien name or analogous power. Both standard and classic Filch are allowed, but only one is used.

Rulebook p13 supplies artifact timing-by-card and general reinforcement rules, but does not print a complete effect inventory of the 72 cosmic cards (it illustrates Cosmic Zap). FAQ rulings are authoritative for specified interactions; unquoted artifact-specific targets, limits and timing still require original card text. Optional Technology is explicitly excluded by task scope. Its unprinted original card effects/membership are not essential source gaps for this task.

No gap is claimed for hand replacement, default encounter flow, losing powers, timing order, flare limits, deals, colony definition: the complete printed rulebook and FAQ directly state these. The no-colony placement, victory timing, simultaneous movement and Zap/non-use rulings are supplied directly, not unsupported component-only gaps.
